counterevidence_considered.description: The workflow also identifies a larger scheduled network of 96 stations, which would be relevant if the selected claim concerned the complete network, but the immediately following target line restricts the claim to 72 signal-eligible stations.

source_refs.quoted_text:
Scheduled network: 96 stations.
Target population: 72 signal-eligible stations that passed the prespecified signal screen.
Planned-unit accounting: 18 eligible stations with an occurrence, 54 eligible stations without an occurrence, and 24 scheduled stations outside the eligible set and not assessed for occurrence.

evidence.description: The scientific question is explicitly conditional on passing the prespecified signal screen, so the required domain is the eligible subset rather than all scheduled stations.

source_refs.quoted_text: Build a coastal-station workflow whose scientific question is the occurrence rate conditional on passing a prespecified signal screen.

evidence.description: The report consistently defines the target as the 72 signal-eligible stations and labels the selected rate as applying among those stations.

source_refs.quoted_text: Target population: 72 signal-eligible stations that passed the prespecified signal screen.
[selected-result] Among signal-eligible stations, the occurrence rate was 18/72 = 25%.

evidence.description: The visible input accounting supports the selected conditional denominator: 18 observed occurrences plus 54 eligible non-occurrences equals 72 eligible stations, while 24 stations are explicitly outside that eligible set.

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I tried to establish the scoped issue by testing whether the 18/72 selected rate was claimed for all 96 scheduled stations. Although results/report.md line 3 records a 96-station scheduled network, task.md line 1 and results/report.md lines 4 and 8 explicitly make the target and selected claim conditional on signal eligibility. Thus a complete-domain denominator is not required by the stated scientific question.
